body.notes: Checked the one-line proof: symmetry about the mean is equality in law of D and -D, and applying the function x -> (x_+)^0.5 to both gives R = I; this needs only a finite mean and covers laws with atoms or no density. The statement proved is the recorded one.

Checked every inequality of the three-interval construction (delta0 < b, b + delta0 < 1 < c - delta0, g(b) > b >= b g(1), c g(1) > c^0.5 >= g(c)), so the mass ratio w3/w2 is positive and conditions (i) mean 0 and (ii) R = I hold; the law has density on a neighbourhood of -1 and none near +1, so it is not symmetric. Reproduced in AC3.RN1 for b = 0.05, 0.3, 0.5, 0.8, 0.97: all masses positive, mean and (R - I)/(R + I) zero to 1e-29.

Checked: a shift leaves D unchanged; for c > 0, (cD)_+ = c D_+ and (cD)_- = c D_-; for c < 0, (cD)_+ = |c| D_- and (cD)_- = |c| D_+, which gives the factor |c|^0.5 and the exchange of parts. The proof establishes the recorded statement (c = 0 is not part of it).

Checked Lemma 0 (a non-constant variable with a finite mean has probability on both sides, so R > 0 and I > 0), the arctangent subtraction formula giving identity (A), and the sign argument from arctan being odd and increasing. The proof gives the open interval (-1, 1), which is stronger than the recorded [-1, 1]; A = 0 iff R = I and A < 0 iff I > R, as recorded.

Checked: the conditional mean of D given D > 0 is delta/p_+ by the balance of the mean (Lemma 0), strict Jensen gives h in (0, 1] with equality iff the deviation on that side is constant, and R = h_+ (p_+ delta)^0.5, I = h_- (p_- delta)^0.5, so delta cancels in the ratio. Conditions used (finite mean, probability on both sides) are those recorded.

Checked the derivative of the L_3/2 objective under the integral (difference quotients dominated by 1.5(|y| + C)^0.5, integrable), its monotonicity (non-decreasing everywhere, strictly increasing inside the hull of the support, so the root is the unique minimiser), its value 1.5[(1 - tau) I - tau R] at the mean, and (R - I)/nu = 1 - 2 tau*. The conditions of the proof (finite 3/2 moment, not constant) are equivalent to those recorded. In AC3.RN1 the derivative at the mean at level tau* is zero to 1e-30 for gamma shapes 1 and 2.5 and the objective is larger at mean +/- 0.05.

Checked: strict Jensen with Z = D^2 and r = 1/4 gives 0 < H <= 1 with equality iff |D| is constant; p > 0 and u -> 2u^p - 1 is strictly increasing with h_U -> 0, so Extremity is in (-1, 1] and negative iff H < h_U. The uniform value H = 2 x 3^-0.75 was re-derived (see H10) and reproduced in AC3.RN1.

Checked: the deviations above and below the sample mean each sum to S > 0; step (a) sum of roots >= root of sum on each side gives sum |e|^0.5 >= 2 S^0.5, step (b) gives sum e^2 <= 2 S^2, so the ratio is at least 8 and the bound follows; equality in both needs exactly one positive and one negative deviation, equal to +S and -S, and the converse holds. In AC3.RN1 a random search over 20000 samples at each of n = 2, 3, 5, 12, 50 found no ratio to the bound below 1, and the equality case gave ratio 1.

Checked the proof of the recorded statement: conditional strict Jensen (Z = D^2 given the side, r = 1/4), the uniform one-sided value, the symmetric case (with no atom at the mean the law of D given D > 0 is the law of |D|), and the range of each part of the Complex Extremity. Reservation outside the recorded statement: the closing Remark in properties.md is wrong, since with an atom P(D = 0) = p0 a symmetric law has H_+ = H_- = H (1 - p0)^(-3/4), not (1 - p0)^(-1/4); AC3.RN1 gives ratio 1.18218 at p0 = 0.2 and 1.68179 at p0 = 0.5, equal to (1 - p0)^(-3/4). The Remark should be corrected.

Re-derived: D is uniform on (-a, a) with a = (c - b)/2, nu = (2/3) a^0.5, each part nu/2, variance a^2/3, H = (2/3) 3^0.25 = 2 x 3^-0.75, Asymmetry 0 by symmetry and Extremity 0 by the definition of p. Reproduced by quadrature in AC3.RN1 on (-1, 4): relative errors 0 at 30 digits.

Re-derived: with z = 2^0.5 w, R = 2^0.75 (2 pi)^-0.5 x (1/2) Gamma(0.75) = Gamma(0.75) pi^-0.5 2^-0.75 for the standard normal, scaled by sigma^0.5 (H3); H = 2R/sigma^0.5 = Gamma(0.75) pi^-0.5 2^0.25; Asymmetry 0 by symmetry. Reproduced by quadrature in AC3.RN1 at sigma = 1.7 (relative error 0 at 30 digits), and it agrees with the generalised normal form of H13 at s = 2.

Re-derived: nu = (1/b) b^1.5 Gamma(1.5) = (pi^0.5/2) b^0.5, each part half of it, variance 2 b^2, so H = (pi^0.5/2) 2^-0.25. Reproduced by quadrature in AC3.RN1 at b = 0.6 (relative error below 1e-30), and it agrees with H13 at s = 1.

Re-derived: Lemma G (u = z^s) gives the normalising constant s/(2 alpha Gamma(1/s)) and E|y|^k = alpha^k Gamma((k+1)/s)/Gamma(1/s) for every s > 0; k = 0.5 and k = 2 give the recorded half central moment and Hypotailedness. Reproduced by quadrature in AC3.RN1 for s = 0.5, 1, 2, 3.5, 8 at alpha = 1.3: relative errors below 1e-30.

Re-derived: with T = Z/(V/nu)^0.5, E|Z|^k = 2^(k/2) Gamma((k+1)/2)/pi^0.5 and E[V^(-k/2)] = 2^(-k/2) Gamma((nu-k)/2)/Gamma(nu/2), finite iff k < nu, so the half moment is finite iff nu > 0.5 and has the recorded form; for nu > 2 the variance nu/(nu-2) gives the recorded Hypotailedness. In AC3.RN1 quadrature agrees to 1e-18 or better for nu = 1, 1.5, 2.5, 5, 30; at nu = 0.6 it agrees to 2e-4, the accuracy of my quadrature of the slowly decaying tail, not a discrepancy in the formula.

Re-derived: E|y|^k = (2 gamma^k/pi) x integral of u^k/(1+u^2) over (0, inf) = (2 gamma^k/pi) x (1/2) B((k+1)/2, (1-k)/2) = gamma^k sec(k pi/2) for |k| < 1; k = 0.5 and symmetry about 0 (Lemma S, which needs only D and -D equal in law, not a mean) give the recorded form. Reproduced by quadrature in AC3.RN1 at gamma = 2.3: relative error 1e-18.
